newsitem.title: INDIA: India United Front puts off steering panel meeting.
newsitem.headline: India United Front puts off steering panel meeting.

text.p: India's United Front coalition has cancelled a meeting of its decision-making Steering Committee scheduled for 9:30 p.m. (1600 GMT) on Friday, alliance officials said.

They said the Steering Committee could meet at any time on Friday or Saturday to choose a new leader to replace caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda now that the Congress party had offered to withdraw its claim to form a government.
But United Front officials said they expected the Steering Committee to meet on Saturday morning, and they anticipated that the 15-party alliance would select a new leader that day.

They said the meeting which had been set for Friday evening had been intended to focus on an impasse created by Congress president Sitaram Kesri's refusal to withdraw a letter to President Shankar Dayal Sharma staking his party's claim to power.
But a fresh letter from Kesri to Sharma in which the Congress leader renewed an offer to support a new United Front leader as prime minister broke the logjam, they said.
At its next meeting, the United Front could focus on choosing a new leader rather than its differences with Congress, the officials said.

United Front officials said they expected a new leader to be named on Saturday and sworn in, along with ministers, on Sunday, ahead of a special session of parliament on the 1997/98 (April-March) budget set to begin on Monday.
The new prime minister would probably seek a vote of confidence within about a week, they said.
